title: TAP-2.5D model package (Ma et al., DATE 2021), original layouts of Fig. 6(a) and Fig. 5(a): independent steady-state FE comparison case
is: The configured MODEL stack and floorplans that TAP-2.5D generates for HotSpot 6.0 (six LCF layers + HotSpot's spreader and sink), transcribed exactly from the inputs the public TAP-2.5D generator writes for the decoded layouts. It is not a physical package.
is_not: our evaluator's result: our own numbers are not provided
status_statement: Our own evaluator's numbers are not provided. Our older values were withdrawn, and our corrected evaluator has not yet passed this same reproduction, so your result is an independent comparison against the paper.

SL:decode.kind: derived from the paper's figures by the SentiLab team
SL:decode.what: die centres and rotations of case A (derived from Fig. 6(a) by the SentiLab team) and case B (derived from Fig. 5(a) by the SentiLab team)
SL:decode.method: vector extraction from the paper PDF (sha256 in PAPER), page 6: the stroked line segments of each panel are grouped into closed rectangles; the panel's frame and scale are read from the four 0.5 mm edge strips that TAP-2.5D draws around the 45 mm interposer; die-sized rectangles, taken in drawing order as TAP dies 0..n-1, are checked against each die's catalogue size; a die's centre is the midpoint of its outline mapped to mm (origin at the interposer's lower-left corner, +x right, +y up); a die is 'rotated' when its outline is the catalogue (width, height) turned 90 degrees
SL:decode.assumption: the figure was drawn from TAP-2.5D's own chip-layer floorplan; the checks are consistent with this but do not prove it
SL:decode.uncertainty: per-coordinate (L-infinity) 0.0007 to 0.0022 mm (cases.*.chiplets[].raw_centre_uncertainty_mm): the extraction error measured on TAP's own panels, whose centres must sit on its 1 mm grid, plus the coordinate times the spread of the panel's three scale estimates, plus half the storage step. It covers reading the figure only; it is not a figure-to-hardware bound
SL:decode.consistency_check: die identity in case B is cross-checked by the netlist: each DRAM sits beside the CPU it links to; routing the decoded layouts with an open port of TAP-2.5D's router reproduces the paper's total wirelengths within 0.1%

paper.citation: Y. Ma, L. Delshadtehrani, C. Demirkiran, J. L. Abellan, A. Joshi, "TAP-2.5D: A Thermally-Aware Chiplet Placement Methodology for 2.5D Systems", DATE 2021, pp. 1246-1251, doi:10.23919/DATE51398.2021.9474011
paper.pdf_verified: PDF downloaded 2026-10-31 from the URL above; sha256 as listed; text read with pdftotext

locations.thermal_settings: Sec. III-A 'Thermal Evaluation', p. 2: six modelling layers (organic substrate, C4 bump layer, silicon interposer, microbump layer, chiplet layer, TIM); ambient 45 oC; grid 64 x 64; spreader edge = 2 x interposer edge; heatsink edge = 2 x spreader edge; convective resistance adjusted to keep the heat transfer coefficient constant
locations.interposer: Sec. IV intro, p. 4: 45mm x 45mm interposers
locations.case_A_value: Sec. IV-C 'Case Study 3: Huawei Ascend 910 System', p. 5: 'the peak temperature of Ascend 910 System is 75.48oC'; layout = Fig. 6(a), p. 6
locations.case_B_value: Sec. IV-B 'Case Study 2: CPU-DRAM System', p. 5: 'our HotSpot simulations show that the system operates at 115.94oC'; layout = Fig. 5(a), p. 6

verification.public_sources: every TAP and HS6 file cited here was downloaded at the listed commit; its sha256 and git blob id are in sources
verification.generator_equivalence: the generated inputs (GEN:*) were produced with TAP-2.5D generator code that is byte-identical to the public files at the listed commit, except passive_interposer.py lines 197-210 (run_hotspot), which input generation does not execute
verification.inputs_regenerated: all 18 GEN files were regenerated from the decoded layouts and matched byte for byte
verification.configs: the dies, powers, connections, placer_granularity and link_type used equal TAP:configs/sys_ascend910.cfg and TAP:configs/sys_micro150.cfg; only intp_size differs (45 instead of 50)
decode_consistency: case A: chiplet centres from sampleL4_ChipLayer.flp equal the raw centres to max |d| = 0.000e+00 m
case B: chiplet centres from sampleL4_ChipLayer.flp equal the raw centres to max |d| = 6.939e-18 m
verification.tiling: L3 and L4 have no overlapping blocks; case B tiles exactly; case A leaves one uncovered strip (ambiguity A4)
verification.citations: every KEY:line citation in this file resolves to an existing line of the cited public file

coordinate_system.origin: lower-left corner of the 45 mm interposer footprint, on the substrate bottom face
coordinate_system.z: from the substrate bottom toward the heat sink
coordinate_system.src_says: the generator writes a die's lower-left corner at (x - w/2, y - h/2) for a centre (x, y) given in mm, in metres, with the floorplan origin at the interposer's lower-left corner

stack.name: heat sink base (copper; fins not modelled, lumped into h)

silicon.where: L4 Chiplet_* and Ubump_* (halo ring) blocks; L2 layer default (overridden by the TSV composite block)

underfill.where: L3 and L4 WS_* fill blocks (gaps between dies and halos); L1/L3 layer defaults (overridden everywhere by blocks)

C4_composite.formula: A = (pitch/diameter)^2 - 1; rho_eff = (1+A)*rho_Cu*rho_fill/(rho_fill + A*rho_Cu), i.e. k_eff = k_Cu/(1+A) + k_fill*A/(1+A) (area-weighted parallel mix), used isotropically
C4_composite.where: L1, single block C4Layer covering 45 mm x 45 mm

TSV_interposer_composite.formula: A = (pitch/diameter)^2 - 1; rho_eff = (1+A)*rho_Cu*rho_fill/(rho_fill + A*rho_Cu), i.e. k_eff = k_Cu/(1+A) + k_fill*A/(1+A) (area-weighted parallel mix), used isotropically
TSV_interposer_composite.where: L2, single block Interposer covering 45 mm x 45 mm

microbump_composite.formula: A = (pitch/diameter)^2 - 1; rho_eff = (1+A)*rho_Cu*rho_fill/(rho_fill + A*rho_Cu), i.e. k_eff = k_Cu/(1+A) + k_fill*A/(1+A) (area-weighted parallel mix), used isotropically
microbump_composite.where: L3 Edge_*, Ubump_* and Chiplet_* blocks; ALSO the L4 Edge_* strips (0.5 mm perimeter ring of the chip layer), as configured (TAP:passive_interposer.py:94-97)

substrate.where: L0 (block Substrate has no material columns, so the layer default applies: HS6:temperature_grid.c:271-274)

TIM.where: L5 (block TIM has no material columns; layer default)

materials.anisotropy: none in the configuration: HotSpot 6.0 detailed-3D uses one resistivity per block for x, y and z (HS6:temperature_grid.c:88-90, 95-97, 822-829)

convective_face.face: top face of the heat sink, z = 0.00846 m, x and y in [-0.0675, 0.1125] m
convective_face.condition: -k dT/dn = h (T - T_amb) (Robin), uniform h over the whole face
convective_face.derivation: r_convec = 0.1*0.06*0.06/s_sink^2 (TAP:passive_interposer.py:156; HotSpot default r_convec 0.1 K/W over a 0.06 m sink, TAP:util/hotspot.config:17,19), so h = 1/(r_convec*s_sink^2) = 1/(0.1*0.06^2) is the same for any sink size (paper Sec. III-A p. 2: 'To keep the heat transfer coefficient consistent ... we adjust the convective resistance of the heatsink')
convective_face.how_hotspot_applies_it: r_convec is divided in proportion to area over every sink node: grid cells (HS6:temperature_grid.c:831-835) and the 8 sink periphery nodes (HS6:temperature.c:444-447), each share in series with that node's full sink-thickness resistance (HS6:temperature_grid.c:829-835, 2333-2336, 1914-1975). The shares' areas sum to s_sink^2.

adiabatic_faces.why: no secondary heat path: model_secondary = 0 (GEN:A/new_hotspot.config:48; HS6:temperature_grid.c:615-646)

adiabatic_faces.face: four side faces of layers 0-5 (z in [0, 0.00056] m)
adiabatic_faces.why: HotSpot grid layers have no lateral boundary conductance (HS6:temperature_grid.c:2220-2226)

adiabatic_faces.face: spreader bottom outside the 45 mm footprint (annulus)
adiabatic_faces.why: spreader periphery nodes connect only laterally and to the sink (HS6:temperature_grid.c:1980-2017)

adiabatic_faces.face: sink bottom outside the spreader footprint (annulus)
adiabatic_faces.why: sink outer periphery connects only to the inner periphery and ambient (HS6:temperature_grid.c:1914-1927)

boundary_conditions.internal_interfaces: perfect thermal contact between all layers and blocks; the configuration has no contact resistances (the TIM layer is the only interface material); no TIM2 between spreader and sink

secondary_path.meaning: off: the r_convec_sec / C4 / substrate / solder / PCB parameters in the config are inert

package_model_used.meaning: off: no fin/fan package model; r_convec is used as given

unused_config_entries.why: with a layer file, layers come from the LCF and HotSpot only appends spreader + sink (HS6:temperature_grid.c:615-658, 402-431)

area_bookkeeping.note: external surface of the model = convective + adiabatic faces listed

hotspot_reference_settings.solver: HotSpot 6.0 (HS6 sources at the commit in commits.hotspot6), grid model, detailed_3D on (TAP:passive_interposer.py:198-207; TAP:README.md:6,23-25)
hotspot_reference_settings.model_type_cli_override: grid (TAP:passive_interposer.py:204 passes -model_type grid; the config's 'block' at TAP:util/hotspot.config:92 is overridden)
hotspot_reference_settings.paper_binary: TAP-2.5D ships util/hotspot as 'a binary file compiled from HotSpot-6.0' (TAP:README.md:24). The SentiLab team's inspection of that binary (it links only libc and libm, with no SuperLU symbols) suggests a build of HotSpot's iterative solver; inferred, not verified by disassembly
hotspot_reference_settings.output_resolution: block temperatures printed with %.2f in K (HS6:temperature_grid.c:1225, 1236)

heat_source.layer: L4 (chip layer) only: LCF 'Power Dissipation' = Y for layer 4 only (GEN:A/samplelayers.lcf:49; other layers N)
heat_source.blocks: Chiplet_i blocks of L4 only; every other block has 0 W (GEN:<case>/sample.ptrace:2; TAP:passive_interposer.py:184-195)
heat_source.in_plane: uniform power density over each Chiplet_i rectangle (HS6:temperature_grid.c:1703-1705, 206-209)
heat_source.through_thickness_primary: uniform volumetric source over the chiplet rectangle x the full chip-layer thickness (1.5e-4 m)
heat_source.through_thickness_variant_S: uniform surface flux on the die's bottom face (z = 0.00039 m) over the chiplet rectangle

metric.paper_statistic: TAP-2.5D's selector: max over every block temperature HotSpot prints (all 8 layers' blocks, plus 12 package nodes), each block in grid_map_mode center on the 64 x 64 grid, minus 273.15 (TAP:passive_interposer.py:209-210; HS6:hotspot.c:548-549; HS6:temperature_grid.c:1162-1237)
metric.hotspot_center_mapping: block value = mean of the 1, 2 or 4 central cells of the block's covering cell range (HS6:temperature_grid.c:1746-1760); the range is rows - ceil(top/ch) .. rows - floor(bottom/ch), floor(left/cw) .. ceil(right/cw) with a 1e-6 tolerance (HS6:temperature_grid.c:241-248; HS6:util.c:55-75). Cells are listed per block in cases.*.layers and per die in cases.*.chiplets.
metric.fe_primary: T_i = T(x_centre_i, y_centre_i, z = 0.000465 m) for each Chiplet_i (chip-layer mid-thickness), volumetric source; M = max_i T_i - 273.15 degC; compare M with paper_target_C
fe_secondary_same_run: T at (x_centre_i, y_centre_i) at z = 0.00039 (die bottom), 0.000465 (mid), 0.00054 (die top) m
HotSpot-cell analogue T_cell(b): sum over the block's hotspot_centre_cells_64 of weight x (area-mean of T over the cell footprint at the layer mid-thickness)
selector analogue: max of T_cell(b) over every block of L3 and L4 (and L0-L2, L5 if convenient), with the block that attains it
metric.fe_variant_S: same readouts with the bottom-face surface source (heat_source.through_thickness_variant_S), finest mesh at least
metric.accuracy_goal: estimated discretization error of M <= 0.1 K

ambiguities.configuration_value: LCF layer 4 'Power Dissipation' = Y (GEN:A/samplelayers.lcf:49); W per Chiplet_i (GEN:<case>/sample.ptrace:2); HotSpot puts each layer-4 cell's power on that cell's single node (HS6:temperature_grid.c:1703-1705)
ambiguities.what_hotspot_does: layer n couples to n+1 through the full rz(n) (HS6:temperature_grid.c:2228-2230, 3396-3397) and each sink cell to ambient through the sink rz, which includes the convection share (HS6:temperature_grid.c:829-835, 2333-2336). INFERRED: in 1-D this equals a continuum stack with each node on its layer's substrate-side face, so layer-4 power enters at the die's bottom face.
ambiguities.treatment: primary: volumetric (heat_source.through_thickness_primary); variant S: bottom-face flux. Report both.

scale.meaning: analytic estimate from the inputs, not a solver result: q''*t_die/k_Si of the hottest die (K), the 1-D scale of this ambiguity

ambiguities.topic: readout point of the block-centre temperature
ambiguities.configuration_value: grid_map_mode center on 64 x 64 (GEN:A/new_hotspot.config:123, 112, 114): a node value, mean of 1/2/4 central cells (HS6:temperature_grid.c:1746-1760); a node has no unique continuum location
ambiguities.treatment: metric.fe_primary (point, chip-layer mid-thickness) plus metric.fe_secondary_same_run (bottom/top faces, cell-average analogue). All pre-declared; do not choose after seeing results.

ambiguities.configuration_value: r_convec = 0.011111111111111112 K/W for the whole sink (GEN:A/new_hotspot.config:17), s_sink = 0.18 m (GEN:A/new_hotspot.config:19); divided by area over every sink grid cell (HS6:temperature_grid.c:831-835) and sink periphery node (HS6:temperature.c:444-447), each share in series with the node's full sink thickness
ambiguities.treatment: uniform h = 1/(r_convec*s_sink^2) on the sink top face (boundary_conditions.convective_face); no fins, no other cooled face

known_differences_hotspot6_vs_continuum: Vertical lumping: one node per layer per cell; link n->n+1 uses the full rz(n) (HS6:temperature_grid.c:2228-2230, 3396-3397); see A1.
Lateral links use the neighbour cell's full-cell resistance (HS6:temperature_grid.c:2220-2226, 3392-3395), not a two-half-cell series.
Mixed cells: a block with >= 95% occupancy sets the whole cell's material; otherwise occupancy-weighted parallel conductance (HS6:temperature_grid.c:74-104, 165-185; HS6:temperature_grid.h:57).
Spreader and sink outside the 45 mm footprint are 12 lumped periphery nodes (HS6:temperature.c:428-447; HS6:temperature_grid.c:1914-2017); the FE models full plates.
One 64 x 64 grid (0.703125 mm cells) for every layer; outputs printed to 0.01 K (HS6:temperature_grid.c:1225, 1236).
These are context for reading a difference; never adjust h, sizes, stack, k, mesh or layout toward the paper.

per_case: M (degC), the primary metric, and the die that attains it
T_i for every Chiplet_i at the die-bottom, mid and die-top planes (K and degC)
T_cell(b) for every Chiplet_i, and the selector analogue (max over L3/L4 blocks) with its block name
field extremes: global max and min (value, x, y, z, layer); max per layer
energy balance: P_in, Q_out = integral of h (T - T_amb) over the convective face, (Q_out - P_in)/P_in; mean (T - T_amb) on that face vs closed_form_checks.mean_excess_on_convective_face_K
variant S (A1): the same readouts, finest mesh at least
A4 optional (case A): void strip instead of underfill
report_back.convergence: at least 3 meshes (refinement ratio >= 1.5, in-plane and through-thickness); per mesh: element type/order, elements, nodes, DOFs, min/max element size, elements through each layer; M and T_i per mesh; observed order, Richardson extrapolation and a GCI-style error estimate
report_back.solver: method; relative residual ||K u - f|| / ||f||; wall time and peak memory per solve
report_back.environment: Python, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-fem and mesher versions; OS; CPU
report_back.reproducibility: one script that rebuilds every number from case.json (record its sha256), plus a SHA256 manifest of script, case.json and outputs
report_back.comparison: report M - paper_target_C per case with the A1/A2 bracket; no pass/fail verdict needed
